claims.explanation: PP-2 is a pyrazolopyrimidine Src-family kinase inhibitor, and its selective killing likely reflects dependence on Src/FAK signaling for survival and proliferation. Lines with high SRC-family activity, especially those driven by SRC amplification/overexpression or by upstream receptor tyrosine kinase activation, should be sensitized, while loss of negative regulators such as PTEN or activating PI3K pathway mutations may provide a bypass and protect cells.

features.basis: direct drug target; Src-addicted lines depend on Src signaling
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT bypass of Src dependence
activating PI3K mutations provide Src-independent survival signaling
FAK/Src complex mediates adhesion-dependent survival; high FAK increases Src-pathway dependence
EGFR activation engages Src/FAK signaling and may increase sensitivity to Src inhibition
annotated PP-2 target; high ABL1 may increase drug sensitivity
annotated PP-2 target; LCK-dependent lines may be more sensitive
annotated PP-2 target; RIPK2 signaling may contribute to survival in some lines
CCND1 downregulation in virtual cell suggests cyclin D1-high lines may survive better
MYC-driven proliferation can increase dependence on Src/FAK survival signaling
